chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabii', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever drinks wine (khamr) after Allah has forbidden it, is not worthy of being married when he proposes (for marriage).'
ai.seo_question: What is the marital eligibility ruling for someone who drinks wine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *kafā'ah* (marital compatibility), this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights that habitual consumption of wine constitutes a moral defect (*fujur*) that disqualifies a suitor, reflecting the Shia emphasis on character over mere lineage. Scholars interpret this not as an absolute ban on marriage but as a strong recommendation to avoid such individuals to preserve the spiritual and social integrity of the household. This ruling underscores the link between ritual purity, moral conduct, and social standing in Shia jurisprudence.
